'''''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order''''' is a [[canon]] single-player [[Star Wars video games|video game]] developed by [[Respawn Entertainment]]. It was released by [[Electronic Arts]] on [[November 15]], [[2019]]. The game tells an original story about [[Cal Kestis]], a surviving [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]], five [[Standard year|years]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Believed dead by the [[Galactic Empire]], Cal remains in hiding for many years. However, he is eventually discovered and is hunted down by the [[Inquisitorius]], and joins up with a [[Stinger Mantis crew|crew]] on a mission to recover a [[Eno Cordova's holocron|Jedi holocron]].

==Publisher's summary==
''From Respawn Entertainment comes a brand-new action adventure game which tells an original ''Star Wars'' story about Cal Kestis, a Padawan who survived the events of ''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith''. Play, and become a Jedi.''<ref name="StarWars.com">{{SW|url=games-apps/star-wars-jedi-fallen-order|text=Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order}}</ref>

==Plot summary==
===Escape from Bracca===
In [[14 BBY]],<ref name="Date note" /> five [[Standard year|years]] after the end of the [[Clone Wars]], former Jedi Padawan Cal Kestis works in a junkyard on the [[planet]] [[Bracca]] scrapping ships from the Clone Wars, but is forced to use his [[Force power]]s to save his friend [[Prauf]] during an accident. Unbeknownst to them, the event was captured by a nearby [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[probe droid]] which transmits the footage to the Galactic Empire, revealing Cal's true identity to the Imperials. The Empire dispatches two [[Inquisitorius|Inquisitors]] trained by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], the [[Second Sister]] and the [[Ninth Sister]], to hunt down Kestis. While being pursued by the Second Sister, who kills Prauf, Cal is rescued by [[Cere Junda]] and [[Greez Dritus]], and flees Bracca aboard Greez's [[Starship|ship]], the [[Stinger Mantis|''Mantis'']]. Cere tells him she is a former Jedi and knew Cal's [[Jedi Master]], [[Jaro Tapal]].

===Discovering the Zeffo===
Cere takes Cal to the planet [[Bogano]] where an ancient [[Bogano Vault|vault]] is located, and hopes that Cal can open it. On the way to the Vault, Cal befriends a small [[droid]] named [[BD-1]], which shows him a message from Cere's former Master, [[Eno Cordova]]. Cordova's message reveals that the Vault was built by an ancient civilization called the [[Zeffonian|Zeffo]], and that he hid a [[Jedi holocron]] containing a list of the locations of [[Force-sensitive]] [[Youngling|children]] inside; Cere believes this list could be the genesis of a restored [[Jedi Order]] that can topple the Empire. However, the only way to access it is to follow Cordova's path and pass his tests.

The only leads Cal has are the location of the [[Zeffo]] homeworld, and a [[Tomb of Kujet|tomb]] on the planet [[Dathomir]]. On Zeffo, they find a clue that the Zeffo had contact with [[Kashyyyk]], meaning Cordova's contact there, the [[Wookiee]] [[chief]]tain [[Tarfful]], may have information about them.

===Journey to the Origin Tree===
On Kashyyyk, Cal teams up with [[Saw Gerrera]] and his [[Partisans]] to fight the Imperial occupation forces [[Slavery|enslaving]] the native Wookiees. Unable to find Tarfful, Cal returns to Zeffo to investigate a tomb when he encounters the Second Sister again. The Second Sister reveals that she was Cere's Padawan, Trilla Suduri, who was captured by the Empire when Cere betrayed her location under [[torture]]. She warns Cal that Cere will inevitably betray him before retreating. Cal learns that he needs to find a device called a Zeffo [[Astrium]] to unlock the Vault before he is knocked out and captured by a [[bounty hunter]].

When Cal wakes up, he is forced to fight in a [[gladiator]]ial arena on the [[asteroid]] [[Ordo Eris]] at the whims of [[crime lord]] [[Sorc Tormo]], leader of the [[Haxion Brood]]. He is rescued by Cere and Greez, and Greez apologizes since the Brood kidnapped Cal in the first place due to Greez's [[gambling]] debts. They then receive a communication that Tarfful is willing to speak to Cal, and they return to Kashyyyk. Tarfful instructs Cal to seek answers on top of Kashyyyk's [[Origin Tree]]. There, he finds another recording of Cordova telling him that an Astrium can be found on Dathomir, but he is then attacked by the Ninth Sister. Cal defeats the Inquisitor and makes his way to Dathomir.

===Trials on Dathomir===
Upon landing, Cal's progress is immediately impeded by the [[Nightsisters|Nightsister]] [[Merrin]], who blames the Jedi for the [[Battle of Dathomir|massacre]] of her people during the Clone Wars, and does everything in her power to keep him away. After experiencing a flashback where he remembers Jaro sacrificing himself to protect him from the [[clone trooper]]s during the execution of [[Order 66]], Cal is attacked by Jaro's spirit, resulting in his [[lightsaber]]'s [[kyber crystal]] being destroyed, rendering it inoperable.

Cal then encounters another former Jedi, [[Taron Malicos]], who sought to learn the power of the Nightsisters and manipulated both Merrin and the Nightbrothers to believe the Jedi responsible for the massacre of the Nightsisters. Malicos offers to teach Cal how to handle the dark power of Dathomir against Merrin's wishes. Cal refuses and flees Dathomir when Merrin attacks both of them, having realized Malicos had deceived her. Cere admits that when she learned Trilla became an Inquisitor, she briefly fell to the [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]], which is why she had cut off her connection to the Force.

The crew travels to [[Ilum]] to find an intact kyber crystal so Cal can build a new [[Cal Kestis' second lightsaber|lightsaber]]. Returning to Dathomir, Cal faces Jaro's spirit again, defeating him by overcoming his feelings of guilt over his master's [[death]]. Malicos again attempts to sway Cal to the dark side, and he attacks when Cal refuses. Merrin helps Cal defeat Malicos, and he is able to convince her to join the [[Stinger Mantis crew|''Mantis'' crew]].

===Recovering the holocron===
The crew returns to Bogano, and Cal uses the Astrium to unlock the Vault and reveal the [[holocron]]. Trilla manages to steal the holocron and escape as Cal is overwhelmed by a vision of the process of her becoming an Inquisitor. Cere reassumes her position as a Jedi Master and grants Cal the rank of [[Jedi Knight]]. They proceed to infiltrate the [[Fortress Inquisitorius|Inquisitorius headquarters]] on [[Nur]], where Cal is able to defeat Trilla and recover the holocron.

Cere attempts to make amends with Trilla, but [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] intervenes and kills Trilla for her failure. Cal and Cere barely evade Vader and escape the fortress by breaking an underwater window and swimming out. Cere falls unconscious from using all of her power to delay Vader, and Cal attempts to drag her to the surface of the water, but he fails in doing so and is doomed to drown. Luckily, Merrin intervenes and saves them from drowning. With the holocron now in their possession, the crew wonders what they should do with it. Realizing that gathering the Force-sensitive children would only make it easier for the Empire to target them, Cal destroys the holocron, deciding that their fates should be left up to the Force before asking the crew where they should go next.

==Gameplay==
{{Quote|Before working on ''Star Wars'' we were working on a different game and it had basically the same pillars that we have in this game, which is thoughtful combat, agile exploration—you know, beyond human—and Metroidvania level design.|Stig Asmussen|<ref name="GameSpot">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/e3-2019-star-wars-jedi-fallen-order-didnt-begin-as/1100-6467511|text=E3 2019: Star Wars: Jedi Fallen Order Didn't Begin As A Star Wars Game|archivedate=20190611021118}}</ref>}}
''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' is a third-person action-adventure [[Star Wars video games|video game]] with a single-player story.<ref name="EA Play SW.com">{{SW|url=news/ea-play-2018-star-wars-jedi-fallen-order-star-wars-battlefront-ii|text=EA Play 2018: ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' Revealed and New Clone Wars Content Coming to ''Star Wars Battlefront II''}}</ref> Game director [[Stig Asmussen]], known for directing [[W:c:godofwar:God of War III|''God of War III'']],<ref name="Stig's Blog">{{WebCite|url=http://admin.respawn.com/stig-blog|text=A Letter From Stig|work=[[Respawn Entertainment]]|archivedate=20190210022059}}</ref> has described the game as having "thoughtful combat, agile exploration, and [[Wikipedia:Metroidvania|Metroidvania]] level design."<ref name="GameSpot" />

The game features four difficulty settings: Story Mode, Jedi Knight, Jedi Master, and Jedi [[Grand Master]]. The difficulty setting impact statistics such as parry timing, incoming damage, and enemy aggression.<ref name="Gameplay">''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' gameplay</ref>

==Development==
{{Quote|My background is melee action, so when they came to us and were like, 'We really like the game you're working out and we want to do at some point, but how would you guys feel about doing ''Star Wars''?' we were like, great.|Stig Asmussen|<ref name="GameSpot" />}}
According to Asmussen, ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' began as a non–''Star Wars'' game and was adapted into the series after various individuals at [[Electronic Arts]] (EA) saw footage of early development.<ref name="GameSpot" /> When his team first met with [[Lucasfilm]], the company was not interested in a Jedi-centered game; the developers then had to work to create a story that would justify the use of Jedi.<ref name="Polygon">{{WebCite|url=https://www.polygon.com/interviews/2019/6/11/18658217/star-wars-fallen-order-jedi-lightsabers-respawn-entertainment-lucasfilm-canon|text=Respawn had to earn lightsabers and Jedi in Fallen Order|author=Dave Tach|date=2019-06-11|archivedate=20190612002142}}</ref> The game was first announced on [[May 4]], [[2016]],<ref name="Stig's Blog" /> and its title was revealed during the E3 press conference on [[June 9]], [[2018]].<ref name="EA Play SW.com" /> An exclusive first look at ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' debuted on [[April 13]], 2019 during [[Celebration Chicago]].<ref name="Mandalorian/Matt Lanter">{{StarWarsShow|blmN_lMJAHk|The Mandalorian Wraps and Matt Lanter Talks The Clone Wars|sw_url=video/the-mandalorian-wraps-and-matt-lanter-talks-the-clone-wars}}</ref>

Merchandise for the game debuted as part of [[Force Friday|Triple Force Friday]], which was held on [[October 4]], 2019.<ref name="Triple Force Friday">{{SW|url=news/triple-force-friday|text=Triple Force Friday Announced}}</ref> and the game was released on November 15, 2019. Pre-ordering the game included an orange color for Cal's lightsaber blade, a unique skin for [[BD-1]], parts for a [[Mygeeto]] Campaign lightsaber hilt, and parts for an [[Umbaran]] Campaign lightsaber hilt. These cosmetic items were later released to all players.<ref name="Amazon-PC">{{Amazon|url=Star-Wars-Jedi-Fallen-Deluxe-PlayStation/dp/B07QL3MH2R|text=Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order – PC}}</ref> [[Fortnite X Star Wars|''Fortnite Battle Royale'']] released a stormtrooper skin that was available for free with purchase of the game from the [[Epic Games]] Store.<ref name="Fortnite">{{EpicGames|url=store/en-US/news/jfo-imperial-stormtrooper-fortnite-offer|text=Buy Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order – Get The Fortnite Imperial Stormtrooper Outfit Free|date=2019-11-14}}</ref>

A book titled ''[[The Art of Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' was published on [[November 19]], 2019 by [[Dark Horse Comics]].<ref name="Art of">{{DarkHorse|url=Books/3005-638/The-Art-of-Star-Wars-Jedi-Fallen-Order-HC|text=The Art of Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order HC}}</ref>

===Music===
{{Main|Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order (Original Video Game Soundtrack)}}
[[Stephen Barton]] and [[Gordy Haab]] composed the score for ''Jedi: Fallen Order''. In addition, segments of music from the ''Star Wars'' saga composed by [[John Williams]] was incorporated into the game. An original soundtrack was digitally released on [[August 21]], 2020.<ref name="OST date">{{ThisWeek|3Hg6c54Aivg|Star Wars Celebration Merchandise, Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Gets Animated, and More!|sw_url=video/star-wars-celebration-merchandise-star-wars-galaxy-s-edge-gets-animated-and-more}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
{{Quote|''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' is one of the breakout titles over the last several years. More than 10 million unique players have joined the game since launch, a rare achievement for a first title in an entirely new franchise. It's a meticulously well-crafted game and it continues to give fans a deeply engaging and original ''Star Wars'' experience.|EA CEO Andrew Wilson|<ref name="MotleyFool">{{WebCite|url=https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2020/05/05/electronic-arts-ea-q4-2020-earnings-call-transcrip.aspx|text=Electronic Arts (EA) Q4 2020 Earnings Call Transcript|author=Motley Fool Transcribers|date=2020-05-05|work=[https://www.fool.com fool.com]|archivedate=20200507020750}}</ref>}}
In an EA earnings call for the period ending on [[March 31]], [[2020]], company CEO [[Wikipedia:Andrew Wilson (businessman)|Andrew Wilson]] commented on the success of ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'', referring to the game as the first title in a new franchise.<ref name="MotleyFool" />

==Continuity==
A [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] miniseries called ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple]]'' debuted in [[September]] 2019, and serves as a prequel to the game.<ref name="Dark Temple">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-jedi-fallen-order-comic|text=''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order - Dark Temple'', a Prequel Comic to the Game, Is Coming This September}}</ref> A sequel video game, ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Survivor]]'', released in [[2023]],<ref name="Survivor Teaser">{{EASWYouTube|4HLDaBGdnLc|Star Wars Jedi: Survivor – Official Teaser|sw_url=video/official-teaser-star-wars-jedi-survivor}}</ref>, with a novel, ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Battle Scars]]'', bridges the two games.<ref name="Battle Scars">{{SW|url=news/new-star-wars-jedi-books-revealed|text=New ''Star Wars Jedi'' Books Revealed}}</ref>

According to [[Matt Martin]] of the [[Lucasfilm Story Group]], some hints at ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' were included in the [[2017]] comic book series [[Star Wars: Darth Vader (2017)|''Star Wars: Darth Vader'' (2017)]].<ref name="Martin">{{Twitter|missingwords|status/1006249459376742403|[[Matt Martin]]|quote=There will be some hints at the game in that series though. But those issues aren't out yet.}}</ref> These connections include the Ninth Sister, the [[Purge Trooper]]s, and the Second Sister, which first appeared in the series' [[Darth Vader (2017) 6|sixth]], [[Darth Vader (2017) 13|thirteenth]], and [[Darth Vader (2017) 19|nineteenth]] issues, respectively.<ref name="Darth Vader 6">[[Darth Vader (2017) 6|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 6]]</ref><ref name="Darth Vader 13">[[Darth Vader (2017) 13|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 13]]</ref><ref name="Darth Vader 19">[[Darth Vader (2017) 19|''Darth Vader'' (2017) 19]]</ref>

In both ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' and the comic book [[Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple 1|''Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple'' 1]], the Second Sister [[pilot]]s a [[TIE/IN interceptor]].<ref name="Dark Temple 1">[[Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple 1|''Jedi Fallen Order - Dark Temple'' 1]]</ref> This seemingly [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]]s information from the reference book ''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]'', which states that TIE interceptors were not produced until [[3 BBY]].<ref name="TIE Fighter">''[[TIE Fighter Owners' Workshop Manual]]''</ref> Though ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' later established that the Second Sister's interceptor was in fact the [[TIE/IN Interceptor Prototype]].<ref name="Galaxy of Heroes">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref> However, another TIE/IN interceptor can be seen during a cutscene when the player first arrives on Kashyyyk. It is unclear if this is the prototype model or the regular model. The ''Galaxy of Heroes'' website provides a partial reckoning of both sources,<ref name="Developer Insights">{{EA|subdomain=forums.galaxy-of-heroes.starwars|url=discussion/253434/developer-insights-tie-in-interceptor-prototype|text=Developer Insights: TIE/IN interceptor Prototype}}</ref> noting that 3 BBY<ref name="Dev insights date">{{EA|subdomain=forums.galaxy-of-heroes.starwars|url=discussion/253434/developer-insights-tie-in-interceptor-prototype|text=Developer Insights: TIE/IN interceptor Prototype}} establishes that the TIE/IN interceptor saw its formal first deployment three [[Standard year|years]] before the [[Battle of Yavin]], which corresponds to [[3 BBY]] according to ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''.</ref> was the interceptor's "official" first deployment,<ref name="Developer Insights" /> opening the door for prior, "unofficial" uses, including prototype tests.

==Legacy==
A [[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order (manga)|manga adaption]] of ''Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order'' by [[Mangado]] and [[Sideranch]] was announced during the "[[Lucasfilm]] Publishing: Manga Mania!" panel on [[Celebration Japan (2025)]] and the cover of the [[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order, Vol. 1|first volume]] and a few production sketches were shown.<ref name="Celeb panel">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-celebration-2025-lucasfilm-publishing-panel|text=''Star Wars: Master of Evil'', a New Darth Vader Novel, Turns the Page on the Sith Lord}}</ref>
